key_insight: Peridynamic thermo-mechanical simulations predict cracking thresholds and damage accumulation in tungsten under fusion-relevant cyclic heat loads.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a pathway to screen plasma-facing materials and assess component lifetimes under severe thermal loading.
method: Use CabanaPD for component-scale thermo-mechanical fracture simulations.
Model cyclic electron-beam exposure across base temperatures and heat fluxes.
Inform simulations with experimental data for recrystallized pure tungsten.
evidence_signal: Simulations compare well with experimental damage classifications from the JUDITH electron-beam facility and identify cracking thresholds across loading conditions.
watch_item: Agreement with electron-beam experiments does not establish predictive accuracy under combined plasma exposure and neutron irradiation.
paper_title: Peridynamic Thermo-Mechanical Modeling of Cracking in Tungsten under Fusion-Relevant Heat Fluxes
